prompt: Last summer my family ___ to Mexico by car.

explanation.rule: Con una acción terminada en un momento pasado concreto (last summer) se usa el past simple: verbo + -ed.

wrong.travel: "travel" es presente; "last summer" pide pasado: travelled.
wrong.travels: "travels" es presente con he/she/it; además el sujeto es "my family" en pasado.
wrong.has travelled: El present perfect no se usa con un momento pasado terminado como "last summer".

examples: We visited Rome last year.
She cleaned her room yesterday.

prompt: I ___ my keys at the office yesterday, so I couldn't open my door.

explanation.rule: "Leave" es irregular: su pasado es "left".

wrong.leaved: "leaved" no existe: leave es irregular (leave – left – left).
wrong.was leave: "was leave" mezcla be con el infinitivo; el past simple no lleva was: I left.

examples: He left the party at midnight.
I lost my phone last week.

prompt: We ___ take the bus this morning because it was full.

explanation.rule: La negativa del past simple se forma con didn't + infinitivo.

wrong.don't: "don't" es presente; "this morning" y "was full" indican pasado.
wrong.wasn't: "wasn't" va con adjetivos o -ing (wasn't happy), no con un verbo en infinitivo como take.
wrong.not: En inglés no basta con "not" delante del verbo (en español sí: "no tomamos"); hace falta el auxiliar didn't.

examples: I didn't watch TV last night.
They didn't go to the party.

prompt: ___ you call your grandmother on her birthday last week?

explanation.rule: Las preguntas en past simple se forman con Did + sujeto + infinitivo.

wrong.Do: "Do" es presente, pero "last week" es pasado.
wrong.Were: "Were" se usa con adjetivos o -ing (Were you happy?), no con el infinitivo call.
wrong.Have: El present perfect (Have you called) no se usa con "last week" y además pediría el participio, no call.

examples: Did you see the match yesterday?
Did she finish her project?

prompt: Which is the past simple of 'buy'?

explanation.rule: "Buy" es irregular: buy – bought – bought.

wrong.buyed: "buyed" no existe: buy es un verbo irregular.
wrong.brought: "brought" es el pasado de "bring" (traer), no de buy (comprar). Se confunden mucho.
wrong.buied: "buied" no existe; además buy es irregular.

examples: I bought a new jacket on Saturday.
She brought a cake to the party.

prompt: The children ___ very tired after the school trip yesterday.

explanation.rule: Pasado de be: was con I/he/she/it, were con you/we/they y sujetos plurales.

wrong.was: "was" es para sujetos singulares; "the children" es plural.
wrong.did: "did" es auxiliar de otros verbos; con un adjetivo (tired) se usa be: were.
wrong.have: En español "tener sueño/cansancio" puede confundir, pero en inglés se dice be tired, no have tired.

examples: My parents were at home last night.
The film was very long.

prompt: Where ___ you at 8 o'clock last night? I called you twice.

explanation.rule: Con you, el pasado de be es siempre were, también en preguntas.

wrong.was: "was" no se usa con you, solo con I/he/she/it.
wrong.did: "did" necesita otro verbo (Where did you go?); aquí el verbo es be.

examples: Were you at school yesterday?
Where were they on Sunday?

prompt: At 7 p.m. yesterday, I ___ dinner with my parents.

explanation.rule: El past continuous (was/were + -ing) describe una acción en progreso en un momento concreto del pasado.

wrong.were having: "were" no va con I; con I se usa was having.
wrong.am having: "am having" es presente continuo; "yesterday" pide pasado.
wrong.had been: "had been" sin -ing no tiene sentido aquí (I had been dinner); falta el verbo principal.

examples: At ten o'clock I was studying.
What were you doing at midnight?

prompt: They ___ football in the park when it started to rain.

explanation.rule: Acción larga en progreso (past continuous) interrumpida por otra corta (past simple).

wrong.was playing: "was" va con sujetos singulares; "they" pide were.
wrong.are playing: "are playing" es presente; "started" muestra que la historia es pasada.
wrong.play: "play" es presente simple; no encaja con una historia en pasado.

examples: We were walking home when we saw the accident.
She was sleeping when the alarm rang.

prompt: ___ I was walking to work, I saw an old friend.

explanation.rule: "While" + sujeto + verbo introduce la acción larga en progreso.

wrong.During: "During" (durante) va con un sustantivo (during the trip), no con una frase con sujeto y verbo.
wrong.Meanwhile: "Meanwhile" significa "mientras tanto" y empieza una oración nueva; no introduce esta subordinada.
wrong.For: "For" indica duración (for two hours) o finalidad; no significa "mientras".

examples: While I was cooking, the phone rang.
He fell asleep while he was watching TV.

prompt: Maria was reading in the garden when she ___ a strange noise.

explanation.rule: La acción corta que interrumpe a la larga va en past simple, normalmente después de when.

wrong.was hearing: "hear" casi no se usa en continuo y aquí es una acción corta y repentina: heard.
wrong.hears: "hears" es presente; la historia está en pasado (was reading).
wrong.hear: "hear" es presente o infinitivo; hace falta el pasado heard.

examples: I was driving when I saw the sign.
They were eating when the lights went out.

prompt: Look at those black clouds! It ___ rain.

explanation.rule: Be going to + infinitivo se usa para predicciones basadas en algo que vemos ahora.

wrong.goes to: "goes to" es una traducción literal de "va a"; en inglés se necesita be + going to.
wrong.is going: "is going" sin "to" no puede ir seguido de un infinitivo: is going to rain.
wrong.going to: Falta el verbo be: it is going to (it's going to).

examples: Be careful! You're going to fall.
She's going to have a baby.

prompt: We ___ visit my aunt next weekend. We bought the train tickets yesterday.

explanation.rule: Be going to expresa planes o intenciones ya decididos.

wrong.going to: Falta el verbo be: we are going to.
wrong.are go to: "are go to" no es correcto: hace falta la forma -ing, going.
wrong.goes to: "goes to" es traducción literal de "va a" y además no concuerda con we.

examples: I'm going to start a new course in May.
They're going to move to Lima.

prompt: I'm not ___ watch TV tonight. I have an exam tomorrow.

explanation.rule: La negativa de be going to es: am/is/are + not + going to + infinitivo.

wrong.go to: "go to" sin -ing no forma el futuro con be: I'm not going to.
wrong.going: "going" sin "to" no puede ir seguido de watch.
wrong.will: "I'm not will" es incorrecto: will no va después de be.

examples: He isn't going to come today.
We aren't going to buy a car.

prompt: A: We don't have any milk. B: Oh, I didn't know. I ___ buy some now.

explanation.rule: Para decisiones tomadas en el momento de hablar se usa will ('ll).

wrong.going to: Falta el verbo be y, además, aquí se trata de una decisión del momento.
wrong.will to: Después de will va el infinitivo sin "to": I'll buy.
wrong.am: "am" no va seguido del infinitivo: "I am buy" no existe. Para una decisión que tomas en ese momento se usa will: I'll buy some now.

examples: It's cold. I'll close the window.
I'm hungry. I think I'll make a sandwich.

prompt: ___ you open the window, please? It's very hot in here.

explanation.rule: Will you…? sirve para pedir un favor de forma educada.

wrong.Are you going to: "Are you going to…?" pregunta por un plan, no pide un favor; con "please" no es natural.
wrong.Do: "Do you open…?" pregunta por un hábito; no se usa para pedir algo.
wrong.Going: "Going" no puede empezar una pregunta sin el verbo be.

examples: Will you help me with this box, please?
Will you close the door, please?

prompt: Why are you wearing old clothes? — Because I ___ paint my bedroom this afternoon.

explanation.rule: Para un plan decidido antes de hablar (por eso lleva ropa vieja) se usa be going to.

wrong.will: "will" se usa para decisiones del momento; aquí el plan ya estaba decidido antes.
wrong.going to: Falta el verbo be: I am going to.
wrong.go to: "go to" es traducción literal de "voy a"; hace falta am going to.

examples: I've bought the paint. I'm going to paint the kitchen.
We're going to have a party on Friday.

prompt: My new phone is ___ than my old one, but it works very well.

explanation.rule: Adjetivos cortos (una sílaba) forman el comparativo con -er + than.

wrong.more cheap: Con adjetivos de una sílaba no se usa more: cheaper.
wrong.cheapest: "cheapest" es superlativo y no va con than.
wrong.more cheaper: No se puede usar more y -er a la vez.

examples: This bag is smaller than that one.
Today is colder than yesterday.

prompt: This is ___ restaurant in town. Everybody loves it.

explanation.rule: Good es irregular: good – better – the best.

wrong.the better: "the better" es comparativo; para el número uno de un grupo (in town) se usa el superlativo.
wrong.the most good: "good" es irregular; no se dice "the most good".
wrong.best: Antes de un superlativo con sustantivo hace falta "the": the best restaurant.

examples: She is the best student in the class.
It was the worst day of my life.

prompt: Today is ___ day of the year! It's 40 degrees.

explanation.rule: Adjetivos cortos acabados en consonante-vocal-consonante doblan la consonante: hot – the hottest.

wrong.the hotest: Hay que doblar la t: hottest.
wrong.hotter: "hotter" es comparativo; "of the year" pide el superlativo.
wrong.the most hot: Hot es un adjetivo corto: the hottest, no the most hot.

examples: August is the hottest month here.
That's the biggest pizza I've ever seen.

prompt: Tom is not as tall ___ his brother.

explanation.rule: Para comparar igualdad se usa as + adjetivo + as.

wrong.than: "than" va con el comparativo (taller than), no con as … as.
wrong.that: En español decimos "tan alto como" o "más que"; en inglés "that" no sirve para comparar.
wrong.like: "like" significa "como" en el sentido de "parecido a", pero no completa la estructura as … as.

examples: My car is as fast as yours.
The test wasn't as hard as I thought.

prompt: How ___ water do you drink every day?

explanation.rule: How much se usa con sustantivos incontables (water); how many, con contables.

wrong.many: "many" va con sustantivos contables en plural (how many glasses); water es incontable.
wrong.lot: "lot" no se usa solo así; la expresión es a lot of y no va con How.
wrong.a lot: "How a lot" no existe; para preguntar cantidad se usa How much / How many.

examples: How much money do you need?
How many brothers have you got?

prompt: There aren't ___ people at the beach today. It's quiet.

explanation.rule: En negativas, many va con contables en plural (people).

wrong.much: "much" va con incontables; people es contable y plural.
wrong.lot of: Falta "a": la expresión correcta es a lot of.
wrong.a lot: Falta "of" antes del sustantivo: a lot of people.

examples: There aren't many cars on the road.
I don't have many friends here.

prompt: We have ___ homework this week: five exercises every day!

explanation.rule: En frases afirmativas se usa a lot of con contables e incontables.

wrong.many: "many" va con contables en plural; homework es incontable.
wrong.a lot: Delante de un sustantivo hace falta "of": a lot of homework.
wrong.lots: "lots" también necesita "of" delante del sustantivo: lots of homework.

examples: She drinks a lot of coffee.
There are a lot of tourists in summer.

prompt: ¿Cuál de estos sustantivos es incontable en inglés?

explanation.rule: Advice (consejo) es incontable: no tiene plural ni va con a/an. Se dice some advice o a piece of advice.

wrong.suggestion: "suggestion" es contable: a suggestion, two suggestions.
wrong.tip: "tip" (consejo, truco) es contable: some useful tips.
wrong.idea: "idea" es contable: a good idea, many ideas.

examples: Can I give you some advice?
She gave me a good piece of advice.

prompt: Can you give me some ___ about hotels in London?

explanation.rule: Information es incontable en inglés: no lleva -s ni a/an.

wrong.informations: En español decimos "informaciones", pero en inglés information nunca lleva -s.
wrong.an information: Al ser incontable no puede ir con "an".
wrong.many information: "many" va con contables; además "some" ya está en la frase.

examples: I need more information.
The website has a lot of useful information.

prompt: I need to buy ___ bread for breakfast.

explanation.rule: Bread es incontable: se usa some bread o a loaf of bread, no a bread.

wrong.a: En español decimos "un pan", pero en inglés bread es incontable y no lleva "a".
wrong.many: "many" va con contables en plural; bread es incontable.
wrong.an: "an" va con contables singulares que empiezan por vocal; bread es incontable.

examples: Would you like some cheese?
We bought a loaf of bread.

prompt: There's ___ milk in the fridge, enough for your coffee.

explanation.rule: A little va con incontables (milk) y significa "un poco, suficiente".

wrong.a few: "a few" va con contables en plural (a few eggs); milk es incontable.
wrong.many: "many" va con contables y "There's many milk" es incorrecto.
wrong.few: "few" va con contables y significa "pocos, casi ninguno".

examples: I have a little time now.
Add a little salt to the soup.

prompt: I have ___ friends in Canada, so I'm not alone there.

explanation.rule: A few va con contables en plural (friends) y significa "unos pocos, algunos".

wrong.a little: "a little" va con incontables (a little water), no con friends.
wrong.much: "much" va con incontables y casi no se usa en afirmativas.
wrong.a lot: Delante de un sustantivo falta "of": a lot of friends.

examples: We stayed there for a few days.
I bought a few apples.

prompt: You look really tired. You ___ go to bed early tonight.

explanation.rule: Should + infinitivo sin to se usa para dar consejos.

wrong.should to: Después de should no va "to": you should go.
wrong.must to: "must" tampoco lleva "to" detrás, y aquí se da un consejo, no una obligación.

examples: You should drink more water.
We should leave now.

prompt: You ___ eat so much sugar. It's bad for your teeth.

explanation.rule: La negativa de should es shouldn't + infinitivo sin to.

wrong.don't should: Should es modal y no usa el auxiliar do: you shouldn't.
wrong.not should: "not" va después de should, no antes: should not / shouldn't.

examples: You shouldn't drive so fast.
Children shouldn't stay up late.

prompt: What does 'You should see a doctor' mean?
options: Viste a un médico por la calle.

explanation.rule: Should expresa consejo o recomendación: "deberías".

Eso sería "You went to the doctor" (pasado).
Eso sería "You are going to see a doctor" (plan).
Eso sería "You saw a doctor in the street"; should no es pasado de see.

examples: You should study more.
Should I call her?

prompt: Tomorrow is Saturday, so I ___ get up early. I can sleep until ten.

explanation.rule: Don't have to = no es necesario. Mustn't = está prohibido.

wrong.mustn't: "mustn't" significa que está prohibido; aquí solo no es necesario.
wrong.haven't to: Have to forma la negativa con don't: don't have to.
wrong.don't must: Must es modal y no usa do.

examples: You don't have to pay. It's free.
She doesn't have to work on Sundays.

prompt: You ___ smoke in the hospital. It's forbidden.

explanation.rule: Mustn't expresa prohibición: no puedes hacerlo.

wrong.don't have to: "don't have to" significa "no es necesario", no "está prohibido".
wrong.haven't: "haven't" es auxiliar de los tiempos perfectos y no expresa prohibición.
wrong.doesn't have to: "doesn't" no va con you, y además expresaría falta de necesidad.

examples: You mustn't use your phone during the exam.
We mustn't be late.

prompt: My dad ___ wear a uniform at work. It's a company rule.

explanation.rule: Have to expresa obligación; con he/she/it es has to.

wrong.have to: Con he/she/it (my dad) se usa has to.
wrong.has: Sin "to" significa "tener", no obligación: has to wear.

examples: She has to finish the report today.
I have to call my mum.

prompt: Yesterday I ___ work late because we had a big project.

explanation.rule: Must no tiene pasado; para obligación en pasado se usa had to.

wrong.must: "must" solo se usa para presente o futuro; con yesterday hace falta had to.
wrong.have to: "have to" es presente; yesterday pide pasado.
wrong.musted: "musted" no existe; must no tiene pasado.

examples: We had to wait for an hour.
Did you have to wear a uniform at school?

prompt: I have ___ been to Japan, but I'd love to go one day.

explanation.rule: Never con present perfect significa "nunca (en mi vida)".

wrong.ever: "ever" se usa en preguntas (Have you ever…?), no en afirmativas así.
wrong.yet: "yet" va al final de negativas y preguntas, no en esta posición.
wrong.already: "already" significa que sí has ido, y eso contradice "I'd love to go one day".

examples: She has never seen snow.
I've never eaten octopus.

prompt: I haven't finished my homework ___. I need ten more minutes.

explanation.rule: Yet va al final de frases negativas y preguntas: "todavía".

wrong.already: "already" se usa en afirmativas (I've already finished), no al final de una negativa.
wrong.just: "just" va entre have y el participio y significa "acabar de"; no encaja aquí.
wrong.ever: "ever" se usa en preguntas sobre experiencias, no en esta negativa.

examples: Has the bus arrived yet?
They haven't called yet.

prompt: Where's Paul? — He's ___ left. You missed him by one minute.

explanation.rule: Just con present perfect significa "acabar de": algo muy reciente.

wrong.yet: "yet" va al final de negativas o preguntas, no entre has y el participio en una afirmativa.
wrong.ever: "ever" se usa en preguntas sobre experiencias, no en esta afirmación.
wrong.still: "still" significa "todavía" y no se usa así con el present perfect afirmativo.

examples: I've just had lunch.
The film has just started.

prompt: We don't need to buy tickets. Sara has ___ bought them.

explanation.rule: Already en afirmativas significa "ya": antes de lo esperado.

wrong.yet: "yet" va en negativas y preguntas y al final de la frase.
wrong.ever: "ever" se usa en preguntas, no en una afirmación así.
wrong.never: "never" contradice la primera frase: si nunca los compró, sí habría que comprarlos.

examples: I've already seen this film.
He has already left.

prompt: Please drive ___. The road is wet.

explanation.rule: Para decir cómo se hace algo se usa un adverbio: adjetivo + -ly (careful → carefully).

wrong.careful: "careful" es adjetivo; para modificar el verbo drive hace falta el adverbio carefully.
wrong.carefuly: Se escribe con doble l: careful + ly = carefully.
wrong.more careful: "more careful" es un adjetivo comparativo; el verbo drive necesita un adverbio.

examples: She sings beautifully.
Speak slowly, please.

prompt: She speaks English very ___. She lived in London for five years.

explanation.rule: El adverbio de good es irregular: well.

wrong.good: "good" es adjetivo (a good student); para el verbo speak se usa well.
wrong.goodly: "goodly" no existe como adverbio de good.
wrong.better: "better" es comparativo y no va detrás de very.

examples: He plays the guitar well.
Did you sleep well?

prompt: I enjoy ___ in the sea in summer.

explanation.rule: Enjoy va seguido de verbo en -ing.

wrong.to swim: En español decimos "disfruto nadar", pero enjoy no admite to + infinitivo.
wrong.swim: Después de enjoy el verbo no va en infinitivo sin to.
wrong.swam: "swam" es el pasado de swim; aquí hace falta la forma -ing.

examples: We enjoyed walking on the beach.
Do you enjoy cooking?

prompt: My brother hates ___ the dishes after dinner.

explanation.rule: Like, love y hate van seguidos de verbo en -ing para gustos generales.

wrong.do: Después de hates no puede ir el infinitivo sin to.
wrong.does: "does" es la forma conjugada; después de otro verbo no se repite la conjugación.
wrong.did: "did" es pasado; detrás de hates hace falta -ing.

examples: I hate getting up early.
She likes reading comics.

prompt: Elige la frase correcta.

explanation.rule: Love + verbo en -ing; con she el verbo principal lleva -s: she loves.

Después de loves no va el infinitivo sin to.
Con she el verbo necesita -s: loves.
No se pone "to" delante de la forma -ing.

examples: They love travelling.
My dad loves playing chess.

prompt: I can't drink this coffee. It's ___ hot.

explanation.rule: Too + adjetivo = demasiado, con un resultado negativo.

wrong.enough: "enough" va detrás del adjetivo (hot enough) y significa "suficiente", lo contrario de lo que se quiere decir.
wrong.very much: "very much" no va delante de un adjetivo.
wrong.to: "to" es una preposición; "demasiado" se escribe too, con dos o.

examples: This shirt is too small for me.
It's too late to call him.

prompt: He isn't old ___ to drive a car. He's only 15.

explanation.rule: Adjetivo + enough = suficientemente. Enough va DETRÁS del adjetivo.

wrong.too: "too" va delante del adjetivo (too old) y no encaja después de old.
wrong.very: "very" va delante del adjetivo, no detrás.
wrong.so: "so" va delante del adjetivo (so old) y no forma esta estructura con to.

examples: The room isn't big enough.
Are you warm enough?

prompt: We don't have ___ money to buy a new car.

explanation.rule: Enough + sustantivo = suficiente. Con sustantivos, enough va DELANTE.

wrong.too: "too" no va delante de un sustantivo; sería too much money.
wrong.too much: "too much money" (demasiado dinero) no tiene sentido con "don't have … to buy".
wrong.enough of: No se usa "of" entre enough y un sustantivo sin determinante: enough money.

examples: Is there enough food for everyone?
I don't have enough time.

prompt: We walked ___ the tunnel to get to the other side of the mountain.

explanation.rule: Through = a través de, por dentro de algo (un túnel, un bosque).

wrong.by: En español decimos "por el túnel", pero by significa "junto a" o "pasando al lado".
wrong.on: "on" indica encima de una superficie, no por dentro.
wrong.for: "for" no indica movimiento; es otra traducción errónea de "por".

examples: The train goes through a long tunnel.
We walked through the forest.

prompt: Walk ___ the stairs to the second floor and the office is on the left.

explanation.rule: Up = hacia arriba; down = hacia abajo (go up/down the stairs).

wrong.on: "on the stairs" indica posición (estar en la escalera), no movimiento hacia arriba.
wrong.for: "for" no indica dirección; en español decimos "sube por las escaleras", pero en inglés es up the stairs.
wrong.above: "above" indica posición más alta, sin movimiento.

examples: She ran up the hill.
Go down the street and turn right.

prompt: The children ran ___ the classroom when the bell rang.

explanation.rule: Out of = salir de un espacio cerrado (out of the room, out of the car).

wrong.out from: La forma correcta es out of, no out from.
wrong.off: "off" se usa con superficies o transportes como el autobús (get off the bus), no con una habitación.
wrong.of: "of" sola no indica movimiento; hace falta out of.

examples: He got out of the taxi.
The cat jumped out of the box.

prompt: Who ___ the window? — Tom broke it.

explanation.rule: Si who es el sujeto (Tom rompió), no se usa did: Who broke…?

wrong.did broke: Who es el sujeto, así que no hace falta did; además, después de did iría break, no broke.
wrong.does broke: "does" es presente y no va con broke.

examples: Who called you? — My boss called me.
Who wrote this book?

prompt: Who ___ you call last night? — I called my sister.

explanation.rule: Si who es el objeto (llamaste a alguien), se usa did + sujeto + infinitivo.

wrong.was: "was" no forma preguntas con un infinitivo como call.
wrong.have: "have" pediría el participio (called) y no se usa con last night.

examples: Who did you see at the party?
What did she buy?

prompt: What ___ at the party last night? — Nothing special.

explanation.rule: Si what es el sujeto, la pregunta no usa did: What happened?

wrong.did happen: What es el sujeto, así que no se usa did en una pregunta normal.
wrong.did it happen: "it" sobra: what ya es el sujeto.

examples: What happened to your car?
Who lives here?

prompt: This isn't my umbrella. ___ is blue.

explanation.rule: Mine = el mío/la mía; sustituye a my + sustantivo.

wrong.Mine's: "Mine's" ya significa "mine is", así que repetiría el verbo.

examples: That bag is mine.
Your car is red; mine is black.

prompt: Is this pen ___ or mine?

explanation.rule: Yours = el tuyo/la tuya. Los pronombres posesivos no llevan apóstrofo.

wrong.your's: Los posesivos nunca llevan apóstrofo: yours.

examples: Is this phone yours?
My room is bigger than yours.

prompt: Those bikes aren't ours. They're ___.

explanation.rule: Theirs = el suyo/los suyos (de ellos).

wrong.them: "them" es pronombre objeto (I see them), no posesivo.
wrong.their's: Los posesivos no llevan apóstrofo: theirs.

examples: The house on the corner is theirs.
Is this table ours or theirs?

prompt: Waiter: What can I get you? — I ___ a glass of water, please.

explanation.rule: Would like + sustantivo = quisiera; es la forma educada de pedir algo.

wrong.would like to: Con un sustantivo no va "to"; sería would like to + verbo (would like to drink).
wrong.like to: "like to" expresa un gusto general y necesitaría un verbo detrás.
wrong.am like: "am like" no es correcto: like no se usa con be así.

examples: I'd like a coffee, please.
We would like a table for two.

prompt: Would you like ___ to the cinema with us tonight?

explanation.rule: Would like + to + infinitivo (a diferencia de like + -ing).

wrong.coming: Con would like no se usa -ing; eso es con like para gustos generales.
wrong.to coming: Después de "to" va el infinitivo, no la forma -ing.

examples: Would you like to dance?
I'd like to visit Peru one day.

prompt: What does 'I'd like a sandwich' mean?

explanation.rule: I'd like = I would like = quisiera / me gustaría.

Eso sería "I had a sandwich"; 'd aquí es would, no had.

examples: I'd like some help, please.
She'd like a new laptop.
